questions.learningObjective: Apply health inequality to a study of health inequality.

stimulus.body: A 2005 health survey of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% reported good health in affluent areas, while 30% did so in poorer areas.

questions.stem: Explain the 2005 Africa finding about health inequality.

answer.exemplar: A 2005 health survey of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% reported good health in affluent areas, while 30% did so in poorer areas. This illustrates health inequality: systematic differences in health outcomes between social groups. A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person, and it distinguishes this idea from competing accounts that locate the cause elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates health inequality: systematic differences in health outcomes between social groups. The 58 percent versus 30 percent split in West Africa shows why this reading fits better than the alternatives.
questions.hint: Think about the social force behind the two figures.
